12 Two different blocks, P and Q, slide towards each other on a horizontal frictionless surface. The
blocks have an elastic collision.
The diagram shows the velocities of the two blocks immediately after the collision.
70 cm s–1
20 cm s–1
P
Q
Which row gives possible velocities of the two blocks immediately before the collision?
velocity of P
velocity of Q
A
10 cm s–1 to the right
60 cm s–1 to the left
B
50 cm s–1 to the right
zero
C
20 cm s–1 to the left
70 cm s–1 to the right
D
60 cm s–1 to the right
30 cm s–1 to the left

hints: Notice the after-collision diagram: P moves $70 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to the left and Q moves $20 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to the right, so find their speed of separation.
Recall that for an elastic head-on collision the relative speed of approach before must equal the relative speed of separation after.
Check each row for two things: P on the left must move right and Q on the right must move left to approach, and the sum of those two speeds must equal the separation speed you found.
walkthrough: Take right as positive. After collision $v_P = -70 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ and $v_Q = +20 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ from the arrows in the diagram.
Speed of separation after = difference of velocities $= 20 - (-70) = 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$. The blocks move in opposite directions, so this is $70 + 20$.
For an elastic collision, relative speed is conserved: speed of approach before = speed of separation after $= 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

Before collision the blocks slide towards each other, so with P on the left and Q on the right, P must move to the right and Q must move to the left. This rules out rows where they move apart or one is stationary.

Calculate approach speed $= u_P + |u_Q|$ for head-on motion. Only $60 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to the right for P and $30 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to the left for Q gives $60 + 30 = 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, matching the required value. This is option D.

A.explanation: P to the right and Q to the left are towards each other, but approach speed $10 + 60 = 70 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ does not equal the separation speed of $90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Approach speed is $50 + 0 = 50 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, which is less than the observed separation speed $70 + 20 = 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ for an elastic collision.

C.explanation: P moving left and Q moving right from starting positions with P on the left would be moving apart, so they could not be approaching for a head-on collision.

D.explanation: P to the right and Q to the left are towards each other, and approach speed $60 + 30 = 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ equals separation speed $70 + 20 = 90 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
